items.text: Kremlin spokesman [[p:Dmitry Peskov]] said trilateral US–Russia–Ukraine talks are planned for the first half of November in Abu Dhabi. Zelensky confirmed that technical-level talks will take place. A US official said the venue could also be Switzerland.
items.notes: Kyiv confirmed technical talks. A US official also mentioned Switzerland. The '~10 Nov' date in earlier reports is not confirmed.

items.text: The White House says First Lady Melania Trump brokered a local ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky so aid can be delivered and civilians evacuated. Russia's [[p:Valery Gerasimov]] and Ukraine's General Staff both say firing stops at 04:00 Moscow time (03:00 Kyiv) on 27 Oct. The White House and Ukraine's human rights ombudsman say the main humanitarian mission follows on 29 Oct. No end date has been given.
items.notes: Sources conflict on numbers: the White House says 1,700–2,000 residents, Kherson authorities about 2,000, and Hromadske over 6,000. The ceasefire starts on 27 Oct, and the main aid mission on 29 Oct (Radio Svoboda, translated from Ukrainian).

items.text: Russia and Ukraine each freed 270 prisoners of war, the first exchange since August according to Zelensky.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched 153 drones and missiles overnight into 25 Oct and that 119 drones were downed. Local officials report at least 4 killed in Dnipropetrovsk oblast. Russia says it intercepted 532 Ukrainian drones. Zelensky says Ukraine received only 24 Patriot interceptors in three months.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: The figures come from the combatants. The attack itself is confirmed by several outlets.

items.text: Ukrainian officials say Starlink is back to full capability after speed caps imposed in mid-October grounded interceptor drones. [[p:Elon Musk]] alleged that Ukraine misused the service for offensive strikes, and Kyiv's technology adviser rejected the claim.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Musk's allegation is Claimed. Kyiv rejects it.

items.text: ISW assesses recent Russian advances southeast of Dobropillia, and outages in occupied areas, including Crimea, after Ukrainian strikes on energy sites.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes

items.text: The Saudi-led coalition says air defences intercepted ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, Taif and Yanbu on 24 Oct and more aimed at Riyadh early on 25 Oct. Saudi civil defence says debris fell in the Mecca region. The [[p:Houthis]] claim hits on airports, an air base and oil facilities, and say Saudi strikes killed 9–11 people in Yemen. Neither side's claims have been independently confirmed.
items.notes: Confirmed means the interceptions; the Houthi hit claims are Claimed. The Houthis deny targeting Mecca and Medina, while Saudi civil defence reports missile debris there. Missile counts differ between outlets. Emirates 24 (Arabic) was translated. Riyadh airport terminals reopened on 25 Oct.

items.text: The navy of the [[p:Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] says two supertankers using an 'unauthorised' route near Hormuz hit mines, caught fire and were abandoned. It also claims seven tankers were attacked or mined around 22 Oct.
items.notes: There is no independent or UKMTO confirmation and no tanker names. Trump has called earlier Iranian ship-strike claims fake. UKMTO did confirm a separate projectile hit near Limah, Oman on 22 Oct.

items.text: The Wall Street Journal reports that the carrier USS George Washington is restocking bunker-busters and standoff missiles for a possible larger attack. Officials say no decision has been made. On 25 Oct Trump said he is weighing a deal against action to 'finish them off'.
items.notes: The WSJ original is paywalled and was not read. Sources conflict: Barrack said a strike was possible that weekend, while SBS reports Trump said none before the 3 Nov midterms.

items.text: Brent crude rose about 3.5% to over $117 a barrel on 23 Oct, up from under $97 at the start of October (AP).
items.notes: Euronews gave $114.73 at a different time on 23 Oct. Sources differ on whether this is the highest since April or since May.

items.text: After two Palestinian gunmen killed two IDF soldiers in Hebron on 23 Oct, the IDF began a multi-day operation in their neighbourhood that includes demolitions. Defence Minister Israel Katz says about 2,000 people have been displaced. The PA vice president called it collective punishment.
items.notes: Displacement figures conflict: Katz about 2,000, local reports 1,500, WAFA over 200 families. Zman Yisrael (Hebrew) was translated.

items.text: Gunmen killed at least nine mourners at a Greek Orthodox church funeral in Karak governorate. King Abdullah II called it a terrorist act.
items.notes: The toll rose from 7 to 9. No group has claimed the attack.

items.text: Ahead of the 27 Oct [[e:2026 Israeli legislative election]], polls give neither bloc 61 seats: about 52 for the opposition and about 50 for Netanyahu's bloc.
Foreign ministers of Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Egypt, the UK, France, Germany and Italy met in Istanbul. They backed the June Islamabad memorandum and called for free passage through Hormuz.
A memo from the US Director of National Intelligence warns that Iran has stepped up efforts to target US personnel abroad. The State Department is cutting staff in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE.
items.notes: The plots are an intelligence assessment.

items.text: [[p:Kim Jong Un]] crossed the new Yalu bridge for a one-day visit to Dandong, China, where he was hosted by [[p:Wang Huning]], who conveyed [[p:Xi Jinping]]'s greetings. State media quoted Kim as pledging closer practical cooperation. The visit comes weeks before Trump's trip to China for APEC.
items.notes: Sources disagree on Wang Huning's rank. No meeting with Xi was reported. Korean cross-check: Aju Business Daily (translated).

items.text: Seoul will raise the 21 Sep DMZ landmine blasts with the UN Security Council and has again proposed military talks on where the border line runs.
items.notes: Pyongyang denies planting the mines.

items.text: Manila rejected China's claim that a 21 Oct resupply of BRP Sierra Madre at Second Thomas Shoal happened 'with China's permission'.
items.notes: The two sides give opposite accounts.

items.text: An explosion, which residents blame on a military aircraft, killed civilians in Sittwe as the [[p:Arakan Army]] closes in on the regional command.
items.notes: The death toll ranges from 6 to 11, and the cause is disputed.

items.text: Islamabad rejected the [[p:Taliban]]'s accusations as 'diversionary' and repeated its claim that 1,327 Pakistanis have been killed this year in attacks from Afghan soil.
items.notes: The casualty figure is Pakistan's claim. No new clashes were found for 23–25 Oct.

items.text: Georgia's Constitutional Court held hearings on [[p:Georgian Dream]]'s bid to ban five opposition parties. Protesters marched in Tbilisi on the 696th day of protests.
items.notes: A ruling is due by June 2027.

items.text: Brazil votes in the [[e:2026 Brazilian general election|presidential runoff]] between Lula and [[p:Flávio Bolsonaro]], who led the first round with 47.0% to 45.2% (electoral court figures). Datafolha's final poll shows Flávio at 51% and Lula at 49% of valid votes, within the margin of error.
items.notes: No result yet at the time of logging; polls close at 17:00 Brasília time. Beware a pre-written 'Lula wins' template page on Portal SGC. Translated from Portuguese.

items.text: [[p:Marco Rubio]] urged Cubans seeking change to form a 'discreet partnership' with the [[p:Central Intelligence Agency]], which then posted contact instructions in Spanish. Trump said warships returning from the Iran war could stop off Cuba. Havana called the appeal desperate.
items.notes: Trump's remark about warships comes from AFP and La Jornada (Spanish, translated).

items.text: The [[p:World Health Organization]] reports 9,704 confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases and 4,687 deaths in DRC, with 9 cases in Kenya and an imported case in Nigeria. Kenya reported its second death on 23 Oct.
items.notes: Kenya's second death came after WHO's 20 Oct data cutoff.

items.text: UN rights chief [[p:Volker Türk]] says drone strikes by both sides killed at least 306 people in Sudan in the first three weeks of October. The UK and 31 partners warned of famine risk, with 19.5 million people acutely food insecure.
items.notes: Most strike attributions are 'alleged'. RSF drone hits on fuel sites in North Kordofan are single-source (Sudan Tribune Arabic).

items.text: Tigray's federally backed caretaker administration urged fighters to disarm, while a Tigrayan commander vowed to fight on. Ethiopia–Eritrea tensions remain high.
items.notes: Battlefield claims are unverified.

items.text: [[p:Delcy Rodríguez]] received the opposition's chief negotiator for the first time after a third round of US-supervised talks. No election date has been set.
items.notes: Translated from Spanish. Round 4 of talks is reportedly set for 11–15 Nov.

items.text: Trump changed which Canadian goods face 50% tariffs from 30 Oct, removing plywood and some paper goods and adding cocoa powder and air conditioners.
A judge ordered pre-trial detention for former presidential candidate Luisa González in a money-laundering case. She calls herself a political prisoner.
items.notes: Translated from Spanish.

items.text: A federal judge dismissed the $LIBRA crypto case against [[p:Javier Milei]] and his sister Karina.
items.notes: Translated from Spanish.

items.text: A week after clusters 2 and 3 opened, Hungary refused to approve screening reports for Ukraine's clusters 4 and 5 at a Council working party. EU diplomats say Budapest gave no reason.
items.notes: Officials expect the clusters to open in December.

items.text: At the 1956 anniversary in Budapest, [[p:Ursula von der Leyen]] told parliament that 'European funding has returned' to Hungary, citing PM [[p:Péter Magyar]]'s anti-corruption reforms. Access to Horizon and Erasmus has been restored, and more funds are expected by year-end.
items.notes: Translated from Hungarian. No amounts were given.

items.text: [[p:António Costa]] confirmed he will table a 'negotiating box' with figures for the 2028–34 budget before a dedicated summit on 26–27 Nov.
items.notes: Euronews gives the summit date as 26 Nov.

items.text: The EU is trying to widen the US–Russia–Ukraine talks to include Europeans, possibly with direct contact with Moscow. A Russian proposal for a Trump–Putin–Xi summit has deepened European fears of being sidelined.
items.notes: Peskov said the talks would stay trilateral but 'nothing can be ruled out'.

items.text: The [[p:European Parliament]]'s Strasbourg plenary debated the October summit and voted on its 2027 budget position and Erasmus+. It reportedly awarded the Sakharov Prize to the [[p:International Criminal Court]].
items.notes: The Sakharov award is Reported. Individual vote results were not found.

items.text: The second Saturday of cost-of-living protests drew 410,000 people according to the Interior Ministry, or 800,000 according to the CGT union. Nearly 1,000 were arrested and there were clashes in Paris, Lyon and Grenoble. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offered to resign over the 17 Oct riots, and Macron refused.
items.notes: The CGT claimed 800,000 marchers. Translated from French. A further protest call is set for 31 Oct and a union mobilisation for 5 Nov.

items.text: France's 10-year bond yield rose above 5% for the first time since 2002, and the spread over German bonds passed 170 basis points. PM [[p:Sébastien Lecornu]] has no majority for a 2027 budget with €43bn of savings. [[p:Christine Lagarde]] said the fix lies in French fiscal policy.
items.notes: Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook.

items.text: [[p:Jordan Bardella]] was re-elected unopposed as leader of the [[p:National Rally]] with 98.98% at its Orléans congress. He presents himself and Le Pen as a ticket for 2027.
Protests took place the same day in Italian cities (9 arrests and 371 brief detentions), Madrid (pensioners) and Lisbon (housing). Brussels shops were boarded up after looting on 17 Oct.
items.notes: The France arrest figures in this piece are inconsistent, so they are not used.

items.text: Italy's cabinet approved a security decree after the unrest. It sends 500 troops to Milan, creates a new offence for groups endangering public safety at protests, and allows preventive detention of 14–17-year-olds.
items.notes: Reports say soldiers were not given police powers after objections from President Mattarella.

items.text: Spain and Italy agreed to lift the reciprocal internal border checks imposed after the summer migration crisis in Ceuta.
items.notes: Translated from Spanish.

items.text: Germany's autumn tax estimate added only about €3.3bn for the federal government, sinking a planned electricity-tax cut. The coalition is split over [[p:Lars Klingbeil]]'s proposal for a higher top tax rate.
items.notes: Translated from German. Partly commentary.

items.text: Regional policy minister Katarzyna Pełczyńska-Nałęcz quit [[p:Donald Tusk]]'s government after the Sejm narrowly rejected scrapping term limits for mayors. Her party, Polska 2050, then expelled her.
items.notes: Translated from Polish.

items.text: [[p:Andrej Babiš]]'s coalition fast-tracked a bill that scraps the licence fee and funds Czech public TV and radio from the state budget, cutting their funding by about 15%. The opposition calls it a step toward authoritarianism.
items.notes: RSF, IPI and the EBU have criticised the bill.

items.text: Parliament approved independent PM Luca Niculescu's government by 280 votes to 58, ending a 169-day crisis. The PSD holds 12 of the 18 ministries.
items.notes: Translated from Romanian.

items.text: Bulgaria voted in the first round of the [[e:2026 Bulgarian presidential election|presidential election]]. Iliana Iotova led the polls, and turnout was low at 16.8% at 16:00.
items.notes: Translated from Bulgarian. No results yet. A runoff on 1 Nov is expected.

items.text: After [[p:Magdalena Andersson]] lost her investiture vote, Centre Party leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist reports to the Speaker on 26 Oct. Fokus says Kristersson may get the next attempt.
items.notes: Translated from Swedish.

items.text: Serbia voted in the [[e:2026 Serbian parliamentary election|snap parliamentary election]]. [[p:Aleksandar Vučić]], who resigned the presidency in September, leads the ruling list against a student-movement list. Turnout was 46.5% at 14:00, against 32.4% at the same time in 2023.
items.notes: Translated from Serbian. No results yet. Tampering incidents were reported by the electoral commission.

items.text: Anti-government protests continued in Tirana. Authorities say more than 300 people have been injured since mid-October. [[p:Edi Rama]] blames foreign actors.
[[p:Milorad Dodik]] praised convicted wartime leaders at Pale, with Serbian and Russian envoys present.
items.notes: Translated from Croatian.

items.text: The Guardian reports that a UK–EU youth mobility scheme may be delayed to protect the 20 Nov summit in Brussels with PM [[p:Andy Burnham]].
items.notes: The Guardian original was not read.

items.text: Romania and the EU accused Russia of a new drone attack after a ship capsized in the Black Sea.
items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Only the headline was read.

items.text: The first Russian diesel cargo to the US since 2023, about 40,000 tonnes, left Primorsk under the deal Trump announced on 9 Oct. A 16 Oct executive order waived sanctions under the Graham Act, and [[p:Kaja Kallas]] says the EU will keep sanctioning Russia.
items.notes: The cargo is due in New York around 7 Nov (Kpler). The CFR piece is an explainer.

items.text: EU gas storage was about 74.6% full on 21 Oct, roughly 15 points below the five-year norm, with Germany near 61%. IEEFA says the EU may need to cut winter demand by 7%. Dutch TTF gas traded above €93/MWh on 23 Oct.
items.notes: The storage figure (74.6% on 21 Oct) comes from an AGSI+ tracker. Prices are Confirmed.

items.text: Trump said he is open to three-way talks with [[p:Xi Jinping]] and [[p:Vladimir Putin]] on 'denuclearisation' as soon as November. A source said they could take place on the sidelines of APEC on 18–19 Nov.
items.notes: The WSJ says Putin pitched the meeting as a way to settle Ukraine on Moscow's terms.

items.text: Tehran says no enriched uranium will leave Iran, though downblending inside the country is not ruled out. The IAEA has no access to key sites.
IAEA chief [[p:Rafael Grossi]] told the UN General Assembly that inspectors must return to Iran and that non-proliferation is 'increasingly fragile'.
items.notes: Grossi is also a candidate for UN Secretary-General.

items.text: In the sixth Security Council straw poll, frontrunner [[p:Rebeca Grynspan]] got 9 'encourage' and 5 'discourage' votes. Every candidate drew at least one permanent-member 'discourage'. The UAE has now nominated Lana Nusseibeh.
items.notes: The straw poll was held on 16 Oct and the UAE entered its candidate this week.

items.text: The [[p:United Nations Security Council]] adopted resolution 2832, drafted by Greece, on protecting children from digital abuses in armed conflict.
